title: Quantile-driven sample selector and runner shim for profile stability
creator: Tomas Rivera
description:
Objective:
Build a quantile-driven sample selector plus a lightweight eval-runner shim to make profile generation deterministic, reproducible, and compatible across our various runner implementations (PyTorch, TF-TRT, and our optimized C++ runtime). This ticket targets two pain points we see during model onboarding: (1) profile instability caused by naive random sampling across heavy-tailed latency/seq distributions, and (2) variance introduced by runner-specific input pre/post-processing differences.

Goals and acceptance criteria:
- Implement a sample selector that: selects samples by configurable quantiles over a workload signature (length, prompt prefix entropy, tokenization buckets); supports stratified quotas and deterministic seeding; and persists a compact fingerprint so samples can be re-derived later. (AC: selector can reproduce a published sample set given the same seed + fingerprint)
- Add prompt-fuzzing hooks that optionally alter non-semantic tokens (IDs, timestamps) to assess model sensitivity during profile publishing. (AC: fuzzing toggle in harness config and a record of fuzzed vs original in artifacts)
- Provide a runner shim interface that normalizes runner-level differences (tokenizer variant, pad/truncate semantics, EOS handling) and emits a canonical per-request metadata envelope to the profile artifacts. (AC: a single profile run across three runners yields <5% variance in median token throughput after normalization)
- Integration with profile publisher: the selector must export a stable manifest (sample ids, quantile buckets, seed, dataset fingerprint) consumable by the profile publisher and the eval harness. (AC: published profile includes manifest and CI job can re-run samples end-to-end)
- Metrics & dashboards: expose sampling distribution, fingerprint collisions, and per-run variance to Console as a temporary dashboard tile. (AC: dashboard links included in PR description)

Design notes and trade-offs considered:
- Quantile sampling vs. stratified random: quantile sampling ensures coverage of extreme tails (long seq/latency), which matters for kernel selection heuristics. We will allow hybrid mode (quantile + reservoir sampling) so teams can prefer distribution fidelity or randomness.
- Fingerprint size: we settled on a compact rolling hash per-dataset split (64-bit) + manifest of top-N tokens for quick debugging. Larger cryptographic fingerprints (SHA256) were considered but add cost to storage and CI diffing.
- Deterministic seeding: seed must incorporate dataset fingerprint + cycle id + user-supplied seed to avoid accidental collisions between runs.
- Runner shim cost: we keep shim as a light pre/post processor to avoid touching runner internals; this slightly duplicates some tokenizer logic but isolates changes. If we later find performance issues we can collapse shim into the runtime APIs.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- M1 (3 days): selector prototype library + unit tests for quantile and hybrid modes.
- M2 (5 days): runner shim interface and two adapters (PyTorch, optimized C++).
- M3 (4 days): prompt-fuzzing extension and harness config flags.
- M4 (2 days): CI integration and sample manifest exporter for profile publisher.
- M5 (2 days): dashboard plumbing + documentation.

Acceptance tests and validation steps:
- Reproduce past published profile ENG-92784 with new selector and verify sample set matches expected manifest.
- Run the same model on three runner adapters and assert median throughput variance <5% and p95 variance <10% after normalization.
- CI job that replays manifest and compares token-level outputs for non-fuzzed samples (allowing fuzzing mode where applicable).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: dataset drift causing fingerprints to mismatch. Mitigation: fallback mode that will attempt best-effort sample reconstruction and mark the profile as "rehydrated" instead of identical.
- Risk: shim adds CPU overhead during large-scale runs. Mitigation: make shim optional and provide a fast-path binary format for large runs; measure overhead in M2.

Notes on compatibility with existing infra:
- This work should be compatible with the profile publisher and manifest schema defined in ENG-92784; we will add a manifest version field.
- Will coordinate with the catalog and profile pinning leads (cc: Ravi Patel) to ensure published manifests can be pinned during rollout.

Deliverables:
- selector library in harness/common/sampler with tests and docs.
- runner shim in harness/runners/shims with examples for torch and cpp.
- new harness config options: sampling.mode, sampling.quantiles, sampling.seed, fuzzing.enabled.
- profile manifest exporter: manifest.json format (flat list + metadata).
- PRs and a console dashboard tile for sampling stats.
